Kinematics.name: Displacement
Kinematics.description: You can use this to calculate how far an object has traveled, taking into account its starting velocity and the acceleration over time.

Kinematics.name: Displacement Definition
Kinematics.description: This formula defines displacement as the difference between the final and initial positions of an object.

Kinematics.name: Average Velocity
Kinematics.description: This formula calculates the average velocity of an object, which is the total displacement divided by the total time interval.

Kinematics.name: Instantaneous Velocity (Limit Definition)
Kinematics.description: Instantaneous velocity is defined as the limit of the average velocity as the time interval approaches zero.

Kinematics.name: Instantaneous Velocity (Derivative Definition)
Kinematics.description: The instantaneous velocity of an object is the derivative of its position with respect to time.

Kinematics.name: Average Acceleration
Kinematics.description: This formula calculates the average acceleration of an object, which is the change in velocity divided by the time interval.

Kinematics.name: Final Velocity
Kinematics.description: This formula calculates the final velocity of an object given its initial velocity, acceleration, and time interval.

Kinematics.name: Final Velocity (Squared)
Kinematics.description: This equation relates the squares of initial and final velocity with acceleration and displacement.

Kinematics.name: Displacement (Using Average Velocity)
Kinematics.description: This formula calculates displacement using the average of initial and final velocity over a time interval.

Kinematics.name: Velocity as a Function of Time

variables.v(t): Velocity as a function of time
variables.a(t): Acceleration as a function of time

Kinematics.description: This formula calculates velocity as a function of time by integrating acceleration from the initial time to the current time.

Kinematics.name: Position as a Function of Time

variables.x(t): Position as a function of time
variables.v(t): Velocity as a function of time

Kinematics.description: This formula calculates position as a function of time by integrating velocity from the initial time to the current time.

Kinematics.name: Relative Velocity

variables.v_{BA}: Velocity of B relative to A

Kinematics.description: This formula calculates the velocity of object B relative to object A by subtracting their velocity vectors.

Kinematics.name: Relative Velocity Addition

variables.v_{AB}: Velocity of A relative to B
variables.v_{BC}: Velocity of B relative to C
variables.v_{AC}: Velocity of A relative to C

Kinematics.description: This formula expresses the relationship between the velocities of three objects in relative motion.

Kinematics.name: Apparent Weight
Kinematics.description: This formula calculates the apparent weight of an object, which is the weight experienced by an object when it is accelerating, in addition to the gravitational pull.

Dynamics.name: Newton's Second Law
Dynamics.description: Newton's Second Law states that the net force acting on an object is equal to its mass times its acceleration.

Dynamics.name: Newton's Second Law (Differential Form)
Dynamics.description: In differential form, Newton's Second Law states that the net force is equal to mass times the time derivative of velocity.
